text: The current Cocoa graphics state over a QPainter (R032). Cocoa draws through an implicit current context with a transform (CTM), a fill and stroke colour, and a save/restore stack. Here that state lives in Python: affine transforms are 6-tuples (m11, m12, m21, m22, tx, ty) composed with plain arithmetic, and a QTransform is built only when a shape is painted (no arithmetic on PythonQt wrappers; unary minus on them crashes FontLab). The base transform maps the drawing space (glyph units, or a view's y-up coordinates) to widget pixels. A context exists only inside a scope ( paint_scope for editor painters, view_scope for NSView.drawRect_ ). State operations outside one raise RuntimeError ; path painting with no destination is a no-op, as in Cocoa. A retained painter cannot paint after its callback.

text: Painters in FontLab's glyph editor: after-native-layer overlays (R032). Native facts (FontLab 9.0.9780; evidence glyport-ui/probe-editor-paint.json ): The editor viewport is the widget workspace.getCanvasForViewport accepts (a plain QWidget named widget here; QOpenGLWidget by preference). The native canvas paints it from an event filter ( CanvasImpl::eventFilter -> _on_event_paint ) and fills it opaquely, so a Python event filter that paints before the native one leaves no visible pixel: before-native-layer painting needs a host hook (R054 note in the L2 report). A transparent child widget of the viewport paints after the native canvas. Glyph-local units map to the viewport as the native glyph paint does ( TextParagraphBlock::_paint_cousins / overlay ): glyph transform * text block transform to canvas units (kerning is already in the glyph transform; only the anchor display adds it again), then flCanvas.mapToViewportF to pixels. The fixture's square edges agreed with the native outline within 1 px. EditorPainters keeps one overlay per open glyph-window viewport (polling for new windows), calls each registered after-native-layer painter once per laid-out glyph matching its layer filter, with a :class: PaintContext whose painter is saved/restored around the callback and only valid during it. Callback errors go to the sink; nothing raises out of paintEvent .
